issues.description: Removing OTLP LoggingHandler from root logger inside _shutdown_telemetry has process-wide side effects
issues.detail: _shutdown_telemetry walks the root logger and removes every LoggingHandler instance. If anything else in the process attached an OTLP LoggingHandler (user code, embedding scenarios, multi-job hosts), this rips it out without consent. Scope the removal to the handler this module installed, or track it explicitly. Global mutation of the root logger to fix a local deadlock is bad taste.

issues.description: _flush_early_log_buffer replays records through the first LoggingHandler it finds, which may not be the OTLP one
issues.detail: The code imports LoggingHandler from opentelemetry.sdk._logs and iterates root handlers picking the first match. Any prior OTLP handler from another subsystem will eat the replay and the real one is skipped. Hold the handler reference you actually created in _setup_cloud_tracer and replay into that. Don't guess by isinstance walk.

issues.description: Unbounded in-memory log buffer with no cap
issues.detail: _BufferingHandler.buffer is an unbounded list. If a job hangs before session.start() for minutes while logging at volume, this grows without limit. Cap it (ring buffer or max bytes) and drop oldest with a one-line warning on flush. A crash-log feature that OOMs the worker is worse than the bug it fixes.

issues.description: Patch does three things; the makefile and worker.py changes are unrelated to crash-log upload
issues.detail: Reordering _queue_msg vs pending_assignments in worker.py is a real race fix. Dropping -n auto and test_plugin_google_stt.py from the makefile is a test-infra change. Neither belongs in a patch titled 'upload logs to server even when session fails to start.' Split into three commits so bisect and revert work.

issues.description: Bare except Exception around init_recording in _on_cleanup swallows everything silently after logging
issues.detail: The except clause catches Exception, logs, then calls _stop_log_buffering only in the failure path. If init_recording raises after partially setting up the OTLP pipeline, you've leaked half-initialized telemetry state into shutdown. Narrow the catch, or at minimum ensure _stop_log_buffering runs unconditionally before re-raising the unexpected ones.

issues.description: Dropping -n auto from unit-tests serializes CI with no justification in the diff
issues.detail: Removing pytest-xdist parallelism makes the suite slower for everyone. If test_plugin_google_stt.py was flaky under xdist, say so in the commit message and quarantine that test, don't punish the whole suite. As-is the change reads like a local workaround that escaped into main.

review.summary: The core idea — buffer logs early, flush through OTLP once recording initializes, force-resolve shutdown_fut on early crash — is the right shape. Execution has two real problems: shutdown rips OTLP handlers off the root logger globally, and the replay path picks a LoggingHandler by isinstance walk rather than holding the reference it created. Also unbounded buffer, also three unrelated changes in one patch (worker.py race fix, makefile parallelism removal). NEEDS-WORK: fix the handler scoping, cap the buffer, split the patch.
